title: Link Each Tree Row Left to Right
statement:
You get the root of a binary tree of any shape. Give every node a next field that points to the node immediately to its right on the same level, or null if it is the last node of its level. Gaps do not matter: the neighbour may sit under a different parent, several subtrees over.

The intended solution uses only O(1) extra memory: no queue, no array of levels. The links you build on one level are what lets you walk the next level.

Our runner cannot see the next fields directly, so after linking, return the levels as you read them by following next: start at the leftmost node of each level, follow next until null, and collect the values. Return the list of levels, top first; an empty tree gives [].

examples.why: 1 is the left child of 3 and 6 is the right child of 5. Their link jumps across two missing children.
Each level is linked on its own. The last level has a single node, whose next is null.

hints: With a queue this is a normal level-order walk: link each node to the one after it in the same level. Now drop the queue.
Once a level is linked, you can walk it with next alone, like a linked list. While walking it, you see every child on the level below, left to right.
Walk the current level and append each child you meet to a list for the level below, using a dummy head and a tail pointer. When the walk ends, dummy.next is the start of the next level.

explain.intuition:
Each level of the tree becomes a singly linked list. The point is that you can build level d + 1 while walking level d, because level d is already a linked list you can traverse with next.

Walk the current level from left to right. For each node, its left child and then its right child (if present) are the next nodes of the level below, in order. Append them to a growing list with a tail pointer, starting from a dummy node so the first child needs no special case. When the walk ends, dummy.next is the leftmost node of the next level. It is the same trick as building a list in a frontend reducer by keeping a pointer to the last item.
steps: Set head = root, the leftmost node of the current level.
While head is not null: make a fresh dummy and set tail = dummy.
Walk cur from head through next. For each existing child of cur, left first, set tail.next = child and tail = child.
Set head = dummy.next and repeat. The last node of each level keeps next = null because each child's next starts empty.
Finally, read the answer by starting from the root and following leftmost heads and next links.
pitfalls: Linking only siblings (left.next = right) and cousins under adjacent parents. With gaps, the neighbour can be several parents away.
Linking the right child before checking whether the left child exists, which skips or reorders nodes.
Reusing one dummy node without resetting dummy.next. On the last level it still points at the old level and the loop never ends.

solutions.title: Level-order with a queue
solutions.idea: Process the tree level by level with a queue and link each node to the one after it in its level.

solutions.title: Walk one level, build the next
solutions.idea: The linked current level replaces the queue. A dummy head and a tail pointer collect the children in order as the next level's list.

followups: If the tree is perfect (every level full), how much simpler does the linking get?
Link each level right to left instead. What changes in the walk?
